short: The climactic final battle of 1914, which halted the German advance to the sea but decimated the regular British Army.
full:
As the Race to the Sea concluded, German and Allied forces collided on 19 October 1914 around the Belgian town of Ypres. The German command sought to break through the Allied line to capture the vital Channel ports, committing newly formed reserve corps. They were met by the remnants of the regular British Army, supported by French and Belgian troops, fighting desperately to hold a salient around the town.

The battle raged for a month in deteriorating autumn weather, characterized by fierce close-quarters combat and localized breakthroughs that were only contained by last-ditch counterattacks. By 22 November, the Allied line had held, but the original British Expeditionary Force was largely destroyed. The engagement established the Ypres Salient as one of the deadliest sectors on the Western Front, where both sides would remain deadlocked for years.
